headline: Elected new 2026-2027 officers, approved a one-time 75% camp refund, and heard updates on Old Mountain Field and Curtis Corner field projects.
summary: The commission approved July minutes and the monthly financial report, and elected John Hanson as Chair, Matthew Fraza as Vice Chair, Joanne Blessing as Secretary, and Will Litvin as Treasurer. It heard updates on the Old Mountain Field and Neighborhood Guild capital projects, a presentation on the Curtis Corner athletic field reconstruction, and a report on Saugatucket Park lighting and Tri Pond Park site furnishings funded by ARPA. The commission also granted a 75% camp refund to Wess Dodge as a one-time exemption and accepted division reports.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 20, 2026 meeting, 3-0.
Approved the July 2026 monthly financial report, 3-0.
Approved the slate of officers for 2026-2027: John Hanson as Chair, Matthew Fraza as Vice Chair, Joanne Blessing as Secretary, and Will Litvin as Treasurer, 3-0.
Granted Wess Dodge a 75% camp refund as a one-time exemption, 2-1.
Accepted the Recreation and Parks Division reports as presented, 3-0.

plain_text:
South Kingstown Recreation Commission  
MEETING MINUTES 
Monday, August 17, 2026 - 6:30 p.m. 
South Kingstown Town Beach 
719 Matunuck Beach Road, Matunuck, RI 
A. CALL MEETING TO ORDER 
Meeting was called to order by Commissioner Will Litvin at 6:42pm 
B. ROLL CALL 
Present: Will Litvin, Matthew Fraza, Joanne Blessing 
Absent: John Hanson 
Staff Present: Jeff Banks, Terry Murphy, Lenka Capek 
Absent: 
Guests: Deputy Town Manager, Luke Murray 
C. MINUTES OF PREVIOUS MEETING 
A motion was made by Commissioner Fraza and seconded by Commissioner Blessing to approve 
The minutes of the July 20, 2026 meeting. Motion passed 3-0. 
D. CORRESPONDENCE AND PUBLIC COMMENTS 
 
E.  Monthly Financial Report 
 
1.  Monthly Financial Report - July 2026 
Director Murphy reported on the monthly financials for August, 2026.  Motion to approve the 
financial report was made by Commission Blessing and seconded by Commissioner Fraza.  Motion 
passed 3-0. 
 
F. Old Business 
 
1. Old Mountain Field Capital Improvement Project Status 
Director reported that the project timeline remains on track to be completed in October.  Park 
activities have experienced minimal, if any, disruption.  A ribbon cutting event will be scheduled to 
celebrate the completion of this significant project.   
 
2. Neighborhood Guild Capital Improvement Project - Status Report 
The Neighborhood Guild project is complete. 
 
G. New Business 
 
1. Election of South Kingstown Recreation Commission Officers for 2026-2027 
The commission established a new slate of leadership as follows: John Hanson was elected as 
Chair, Matthew Fraza was elected as Vice Chair, Joanne Blessing was elected as Secretary and Will 
Litvin was elected as Treasurer. The motion to approve this slate was made by Commissioner 
Blessing and seconded by Commissioner Fraza, passing  3-0.
2. Presentation on School Department Athletic Field Reconstruction, Entry Drive and Parking at 
Curtis Corner - — Project Details and Timeline 
The commission received a detailed presentation  from Deputy Town Manager Murray on the CCMS 
athletic field reconstruction, including plans for new lighting, parking, and potential "add 
alternates" for pavement versus grass parking. 
 
3. Report on Saugatucket Park Lighting and Site Furnishings for Tri Pond Park and Bike Path 
Between Comfort Station and Route 108 Crossing in Peace Dale — Funding through American 
Rescue Plan Act 
 
Deputy Town Manager Murray provided information about proposed amenities for Saugatucket 
Park, Tri Pond Park, and the Bike path. 
Project Scope: The town is reallocating ARPA funds, originally intended for a facade improvement 
program, to install new lighting at Saugatucket Park. 
o Design: The project involves installing 23 period-style, colonial-look fixtures.  
o Implementation: A two-pronged approach is being used: the town is purchasing the lights 
directly through a state price agreement, while a separate contractor will be hired via a 
performance-based bid to handle the electrical work, wiring, and footings. 
o Site Furnishings for Tri Pond / Peace Dale Area): 
o Status of Funds: Following successful installations of benches and trash receptacles 
on Main Street, Saugatucket Park, and the Riverwalk, approximately $50,000 in ARPA funds 
remains to be allocated. 
o Future Plans: The next phase targets the Peace Dale area, specifically the dam and reservoir 
surroundings. 
Proposed Improvements: The plan includes adding four or five picnic tables to the dam area.  
 
4. Request from Wess Dodge for consideration of waiver of camp refund policy   
The commission discussed a camp registration refund request by Wess Dodge. After discussion 
and determining that the partial cancellation would not negatively impact their programming, the 
commission moved to grant a 75% refund as a one-time exemption.  Motion made by 
commissioner Fraza and seconded by Commissioner Litvin.  Motion passed 2-1. Fraza – aye, Litvin- 
aye, Blessing - nay 
H.    DIVISION REPORTS 
1. Recreation Division: Supt. Capek reported on July programs and Town Beach operations noting that 
Camp registration saw strong numbers, with 1,896 total registrations throughout July and a successful 
counselor-in-training program. 
 
2. Parks Division: Supt. Banks reported on July projects and overall work activity of the parks Division 
noting that Staff have been active with safety improvements at the Nancy Brown playground, 
maintenance at the Wakefield Riverwalk, and ongoing grooming at the Town Beach   
A motion to accept the Divisional reports as presented was made by Commissioner Blessing and 
seconded by Commissioner Fraza. Motion passed 3-0. 
I. NEXT MEETING 
The next meeting of the Commission is scheduled for Monday, September 21 , 2026, at 6:30 p.m. at the 
The Neighborhood Guild. 
J.     ADJOURNMENT 
A motion to adjourn was made at 8:09pm by Commissioner Fraza and seconded by Commissioner 
Blessing. Motion passed 3-0.
